cards.name: IVGArrowHeadOptions
cards.summary: Size, offset, rotation and mirroring settings for the arrowhead at one end of an outline (the Arrowhead Attributes values): Length and Width scale the head, OffsetX / OffsetY nudge it in percent of its own size, RotationAngle turns it, FlipHorizontal / FlipVertical mirror it. It does not choose which arrowhead is drawn; that is Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow.
use_for: longer or slimmer arrowheads on callout and leader lines
matching arrowhead size across every connector in an infographic or flow chart
mirroring or rotating a custom arrowhead without redrawing it
copying one line's arrowhead settings to other lines
avoid: choosing the arrowhead shape: set Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow to an ArrowHead from Application.ArrowHeads instead
lines with no arrowhead assigned: the options have nothing visible to change
cards.how: Per-end arrowhead settings of an outline. Read from Shape.Outline.StartArrowOptions / EndArrowOptions (read/write, propput in the typelib), or build a free-standing one with ActiveDocument.CreateArrowHeadOptions(Length, Width, OffsetX, OffsetY, RotationAngle, FlipHorizontal, FlipVertical) and assign it to an outline. GetCopy / CopyAssign move settings between lines.

key_members.name: Length
key_members.use: horizontal size of the arrowhead (along the line)

key_members.name: Width
key_members.use: vertical size of the arrowhead (across the line)

key_members.name: OffsetX
key_members.use: shift along the line, in percent of the arrowhead length

key_members.name: OffsetY
key_members.use: shift across the line, in percent of the arrowhead width

key_members.name: RotationAngle
key_members.use: rotation of the head around its origin point

key_members.name: FlipHorizontal
key_members.use: mirror the head horizontally

key_members.name: FlipVertical
key_members.use: mirror the head vertically

key_members.name: Flip
key_members.use: mirror by a cdrFlipAxes value (cdrFlipHorizontal / cdrFlipVertical / cdrFlipBoth)

key_members.name: GetCopy
key_members.use: detached copy to edit and assign elsewhere

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: take all settings from another ArrowHeadOptions

gotchas: FlipVerical (misspelled, hidden) is a legacy alias of FlipVertical; use FlipVertical
OffsetX / OffsetY are percentages of the arrowhead's length / width, not document units
whether editing the object returned by Outline.StartArrowOptions changes the line in place is not confirmed; the safe pattern is GetCopy, edit, assign back (unverified)
Outline.StartArrowOptions / EndArrowOptions are propput in the typelib: in VBA assign without Set
Length / Width are in document units (ActiveDocument.Unit) like other CorelDRAW sizes (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, o As ArrowHeadOptions
Set s = ActiveShape  ' a line that already has an end arrowhead
Set o = s.Outline.EndArrowOptions.GetCopy
o.Length = 0.4: o.Width = 0.2
o.RotationAngle = 15
s.Outline.EndArrowOptions = o

review.changes: none

cards.name: IVGArrowHeads
cards.summary: The application-wide list of arrowhead shapes (the choices in the Outline Pen arrowhead pickers), 1-based. Scripts take an ArrowHead from it to put on a line's start or end, and can add, replace or remove custom arrowheads in that global list.
use_for: putting a chosen arrowhead on leader lines, callouts and flow-chart connectors
registering a custom arrowhead drawn as a curve so every document can use it
listing the available arrowheads to pick one by name
avoid: sizing or rotating the head on one line: that is Outline.StartArrowOptions / EndArrowOptions (ArrowHeadOptions)
Remove / Replace on a shared workstation: they change the user's global arrowhead list, not just the document
cards.how: Collection returned by Application.ArrowHeads. Item(Index) (default member, base 1) gives an ArrowHead to assign to Shape.Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow; Add(ArrowHead) takes one built with ActiveDocument.CreateArrowHead(curve) or CreateArrowHead2(curve, name) and returns the copy stored in the global list.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: arrowhead by 1-based position (default member)

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of arrowheads in the list

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets VBA For Each walk the list

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: add a custom ArrowHead to the global list; returns the stored arrowhead

key_members.name: Replace
key_members.use: swap the arrowhead at an index for another

key_members.name: Remove
key_members.use: delete the arrowhead at an index from the global list

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the Application (not a document)

key_members.name: Application
key_members.use: the CorelDRAW application

gotchas: Item takes a position, and Remove probably shifts every later position (unverified); find an arrowhead by ArrowHead.Name / DisplayName rather than hard-coding a number
Add / Remove / Replace edit the global list shared by all documents, which is kept between sessions (unverified)
Outline.StartArrow / EndArrow are propput in the typelib: in VBA assign without Set
a custom arrowhead made with CreateArrowHead is usable on a line without Add; Add only makes it appear in the pickers (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim ah As ArrowHead
For Each ah In Application.ArrowHeads
  Debug.Print ah.Index, ah.DisplayName
Next ah
ActiveShape.Outline.EndArrow = Application.ArrowHeads(3)

review.changes: marked the claim that Remove shifts later positions as unverified

cards.name: IVGBBoxSnapPoint
cards.summary: The bounding-box part of a snap point: when a SnapPoint is one of a shape's bounding-box handles, BBox.Type tells which one (a corner, an edge midpoint or the centre, as a cdrReferencePoint).
use_for: anchoring connector or dimension lines to a chosen corner or edge midpoint of a box in a diagram
telling which bounding-box handle a found snap point belongs to
attaching callout leaders to the top-middle or bottom-middle of labels
avoid: reading the point's coordinates: PositionX / PositionY are on the parent SnapPoint
node, edge or user snap points: BBox only applies when SnapPoint.Type is cdrSnapPointBBox
cards.how: Reached as SnapPoint.BBox on a snap point whose Type = cdrSnapPointBBox. Get such snap points from Shape.SnapPoints.BBox(cdrTopLeft ...) or Shape.SnapPointsOfType(cdrSnapPointBBox); the SnapPoint itself (not this object) is what Layer.CreateConnector / CreateLinearDimension take.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: which handle: cdrTopRight, cdrTopMiddle, cdrTopLeft, cdrMiddleLeft, cdrBottomLeft, cdrBottomMiddle, cdrBottomRight, cdrMiddleRight or cdrCenter

gotchas: only one member: position, shape and selection live on the parent SnapPoint
cdrReferencePoint numbering starts at cdrTopRight = 1 and runs counter-clockwise to cdrMiddleRight = 8, with cdrCenter = 9; TopLeft is 3, not 1
SnapPoint.BBox on a snap point that is not a bounding-box point returns Nothing or raises (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim sp As SnapPoint
For Each sp In ActiveShape.SnapPointsOfType(cdrSnapPointBBox)
  Debug.Print sp.BBox.Type, sp.PositionX, sp.PositionY
Next sp

review.changes: none

cards.name: IVGBitmap
cards.summary: The pixel side of a bitmap object on the page: pixel size, resolution, colour mode, link status and crop path, plus the operations a script runs on it (resample, change colour mode, apply a bitmap effect, crop, trace to vectors, save out, read or replace the pixel data).
use_for: checking placed photos for effective resolution before print
converting RGB images to CMYK or grayscale for a print job
downsampling oversized images to shrink the file
embedding linked images before packaging a file
auto-tracing a logo or line-art scan to vectors
applying a bitmap effect to a photo from a script
avoid: vector shapes: rasterise first with Shape.ConvertToBitmapEx, then use Shape.Bitmap
size or position on the page: those are Shape properties (SizeWidth here is pixels, not page units)
heavy photo retouching: do it in Photoshop or Corel PHOTO-PAINT and relink
cards.how: Reached as Shape.Bitmap on a shape whose Type = cdrBitmapShape (also EPS.PreviewBitmap). Read-only facts (SizeWidth / SizeHeight in pixels, ResolutionX / Y, Mode, ExternallyLinked) plus methods that change the image in place: Resample, ConvertTo, ConvertToBW / ConvertToPaletted / ConvertToDuotone, ApplyBitmapEffect, Crop, Trace, SetImageData.

key_members.name: SizeWidth
key_members.use: width in pixels

key_members.name: SizeHeight
key_members.use: height in pixels

key_members.name: ResolutionX
key_members.use: horizontal resolution (dpi)

key_members.name: ResolutionY
key_members.use: vertical resolution (dpi)

key_members.name: Mode
key_members.use: colour mode as cdrImageType (cdrRGBColorImage, cdrCMYKColorImage ...)

key_members.name: ConvertTo
key_members.use: change colour mode, e.g. to cdrCMYKColorImage or cdrGrayscaleImage

key_members.name: Resample
key_members.use: change pixel size and / or resolution, optional anti-aliasing

key_members.name: ApplyBitmapEffect
key_members.use: run a bitmap effect from its command string, with an undo label

key_members.name: ExternallyLinked
key_members.use: True when the pixels live in an external file

key_members.name: LinkFileName
key_members.use: path of the linked file

key_members.name: ResolveLink
key_members.use: embed a linked bitmap

key_members.name: UpdateLink
key_members.use: reload a linked bitmap from its file

key_members.name: Crop
key_members.use: crop the pixels to the edited crop path

key_members.name: CropEnvelope
key_members.use: the clipping path curve

key_members.name: Trace
key_members.use: start PowerTRACE; returns TraceSettings (call Finish to create the vectors)

key_members.name: SaveAs
key_members.use: write the bitmap to a file through an export filter

key_members.name: Image
key_members.use: pixel data as an Image object

key_members.name: ImageAlpha
key_members.use: transparency mask as an Image object (Nothing when opaque)

key_members.name: SetImageData
key_members.use: replace pixels and optional alpha mask

key_members.name: Transparent
key_members.use: True when the bitmap has transparency

gotchas: SizeWidth / SizeHeight are pixel dimensions; the size on the page is Shape.SizeWidth / SizeHeight in document units
Trace returns a TraceSettings object; nothing is created until its Finish is called, which returns the new ShapeRange
ApplyBitmapEffect takes an internal effect command string, not the menu name; record the effect with the macro recorder to get the exact string (unverified)
SaveAs returns an export filter object; the file is written when Finish is called on it (unverified)
Resample, ConvertTo and ConvertToBW change the embedded pixels destructively; duplicate the shape first if the original may be needed
Shape.Bitmap on a non-bitmap shape fails; check Shape.Type = cdrBitmapShape first (unverified)
Crop only does something after the crop envelope was edited (see Cropped / CropEnvelopeModified) (unverified)

ConvertToBW(RenderType, Intensity, Threshold, Halftone, Angle, Size): ConvertToBW(5, 0, 128, 2, 45, 16) (RenderType 5 halftone, Halftone 2 line) gives a diagonal line screen whose line thickness follows the tone (engraving); ConvertToBW(0, 0, 112, 0, 0, 0) (RenderType 0 line art, a threshold) gives solid black-or-paper two-tone line art (woodcut) (plan runs 2026-10-15 (poster_print.line_engraving, poster_print.woodcut)).
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
For Each s In ActivePage.Shapes
  If s.Type = cdrBitmapShape Then
    If s.Bitmap.ExternallyLinked Then s.Bitmap.ResolveLink
    If s.Bitmap.Mode = cdrRGBColorImage Then s.Bitmap.ConvertTo cdrCMYKColorImage
    Debug.Print s.Name, s.Bitmap.ResolutionX & " dpi"
  End If
Next s

review.changes: none

cards.name: IVGBSpline
cards.summary: A B-spline curve definition: a list of control points that the smooth curve is pulled toward (it passes through a point only when that point is clamped) plus an open / closed flag. It is the scripting form of curves drawn with the B-Spline tool.
use_for: generating smooth organic outlines (waves, blobs, flowing ribbons) from a few computed points
procedural wavy dividers and swooshes for layouts
reading the control polygon of a B-Spline-tool curve
avoid: paths that must hit exact corners and points: build a Bezier curve (Layer.CreateCurve) instead
editing an existing shape's spline in place: Shape.BSpline is read-only, draw a new shape from an edited copy
cards.how: Built free-standing with ActiveDocument.CreateBSpline(NumControlPoints, Closed), edited through ControlPoints, then drawn with ActiveLayer.CreateBSpline(bspline), which returns the new Shape. Shape.BSpline returns a read-only BSpline of an existing B-spline curve.

key_members.name: ControlPoints
key_members.use: the BSplineControlPoints list

key_members.name: Closed
key_members.use: True for a closed loop, False for an open curve

key_members.name: InsertControlPoint
key_members.use: insert one point (x, y, clamped) before an index

key_members.name: InsertControlPoints
key_members.use: insert several identical points before an index

key_members.name: GetCopy
key_members.use: detached, editable copy

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: take all points and the closed flag from another BSpline

gotchas: Shape.BSpline is documented as read-only: edit a GetCopy and draw it with Layer.CreateBSpline; how to write it back onto the same shape is not confirmed (unverified)
ControlPoints.Resize adds points at (0, 0); new points from CreateBSpline probably also start there, so set every position before drawing (unverified for CreateBSpline)
unclamped end points of an open spline sit off the curve; clamp them if the curve must start and end exactly on them (unverified)
whether control-point indices are 0- or 1-based is not confirmed; use For Each or First / Last (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim bs As BSpline, cp As BSplineControlPoint, i As Long
Set bs = ActiveDocument.CreateBSpline(6, False)
For Each cp In bs.ControlPoints
  cp.SetPosition i, (i Mod 2) * 1.5: i = i + 1
Next cp
ActiveLayer.CreateBSpline bs

review.changes: none

cards.name: IVGBSplineControlPoint
cards.summary: One control point of a B-spline: its x / y position and whether it is clamped (a clamped point forces the curve through it with a cusp; an unclamped one only pulls the curve toward it).
use_for: placing computed points for smooth procedural curves (sine waves, blobs)
pinning a B-spline to exact spots by clamping points
nudging part of a smooth wave without redrawing it
avoid: Bezier nodes with handles: those are the Curve's nodes and segments, not B-spline control points
cards.how: Item of BSpline.ControlPoints (Item(Index), First, Last or For Each). SetPosition / SetProperties place it absolutely, Move shifts it by a distance, Delete removes it, Index reports its position in the list.

key_members.name: x
key_members.use: horizontal position

key_members.name: y
key_members.use: vertical position

key_members.name: Clamped
key_members.use: True: the curve passes through this point with a cusp

key_members.name: SetPosition
key_members.use: set x and y in one call (absolute)

key_members.name: SetProperties
key_members.use: set x, y and Clamped in one call

key_members.name: GetPosition
key_members.use: read x and y through ByRef arguments

key_members.name: Move
key_members.use: shift by a distance (relative)

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: remove the point from the spline

key_members.name: Index
key_members.use: position of the point in the list

gotchas: Move(x, y) is relative (moves by a distance); SetPosition(x, y) is absolute
GetPosition x / y are out (ByRef) parameters in the typelib: in VBA pass Double variables; in Python win32com they should come back as a returned tuple (unverified)
edits only matter on a BSpline that is then drawn with Layer.CreateBSpline; a BSpline from Shape.BSpline is read-only
coordinates are in document units (ActiveDocument.Unit) (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim bs As BSpline, cp As BSplineControlPoint
Set bs = ActiveDocument.CreateBSpline(3, False)
bs.ControlPoints.First.SetProperties 0, 0, True
bs.ControlPoints.Last.SetProperties 4, 0, True
For Each cp In bs.ControlPoints
  If Not cp.Clamped Then cp.SetPosition 2, 3
Next cp
ActiveLayer.CreateBSpline bs

review.changes: GetPosition gotcha now states the out-parameter flags read from the typelib; the Python tuple return stays unverified

cards.name: IVGBSplineControlPoints
cards.summary: The ordered list of control points of one B-spline, with First / Last shortcuts, Count, indexed access and Resize to grow or shrink the list.
use_for: looping over a spline's points to lay out a computed wave or blob
setting how many points a generated spline has before positioning them
reading a B-Spline-tool curve's control polygon
avoid: adding one point at a given place and position: use BSpline.InsertControlPoint; Resize only adds points at (0, 0)
cards.how: BSpline.ControlPoints. Item(Index) is the default member; For Each works through _NewEnum; Resize(HowMany) sets the number of points.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of control points

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: a control point by index (default member)

key_members.name: First
key_members.use: the first control point

key_members.name: Last
key_members.use: the last control point

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets VBA For Each walk the points

key_members.name: Resize
key_members.use: set the number of points; added points sit at (0, 0)

gotchas: Resize adds new control points at (0, 0) (per the typelib); position them before drawing
Resize to fewer points presumably drops points from the end (unverified)
index base of Item is not confirmed (most CorelDRAW collections are 1-based); First / Last and For Each avoid the question (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim bs As BSpline, cp As BSplineControlPoint, i As Long
Set bs = ActiveDocument.CreateBSpline(2, True)
bs.ControlPoints.Resize 8
For Each cp In bs.ControlPoints
  cp.SetPosition 2 * Cos(i * 0.785), 2 * Sin(i * 0.785): i = i + 1
Next cp
ActiveLayer.CreateBSpline bs

review.changes: none

cards.name: IVGClipboard
cards.summary: A view of the Windows clipboard as CorelDRAW sees it: whether it holds content CorelDRAW can paste, whether a named data format is present, and Clear to empty it. Copying and pasting themselves are Shape.Copy and Layer.Paste.
use_for: checking that a copy step worked before pasting artwork into another document
guarding a paste of content copied from another app (only paste when a usable format is present)
clearing large copied artwork from the clipboard after a batch job
avoid: moving shapes between layers or documents inside one script: Shape.CopyToLayer / Duplicate avoid the shared system clipboard
unattended jobs running beside other clipboard users: the clipboard is global and can be overwritten mid-run
cards.how: Application.Clipboard. Valid and Empty are flags, DataPresent(FormatName) tests one clipboard format, Clear empties it. Content goes there with Shape.Copy / ShapeRange.Copy and comes back with Layer.Paste, PasteEx or PasteSpecial.

key_members.name: Valid
key_members.use: True when the clipboard holds content CorelDRAW can use

key_members.name: Empty
key_members.use: content flag (see gotchas for its sense)

key_members.name: DataPresent
key_members.use: True when the named clipboard format is present

key_members.name: Clear
key_members.use: empty the clipboard

key_members.name: Application
key_members.use: the CorelDRAW application

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the owning object (the Application)

gotchas: Clear empties the shared Windows clipboard, so other applications lose its content too (unverified)
the typelib describes Empty as checking whether the clipboard has content, which reads like the opposite of its name; test its sense against Valid before relying on it (unverified)
DataPresent needs the exact registered clipboard format name; which names this version (25.1) registers is not in the harvest (unverified)
there is no member to put data on the clipboard; use Shape.Copy / ShapeRange.Copy
cards.example:
ActiveShape.Copy
If Application.Clipboard.Valid Then
  ActiveLayer.Paste
End If
Application.Clipboard.Clear

review.changes: replaced "CorelDRAW 2024" (not in the batch) with version 25.1; marked the Clear-affects-all-apps gotcha unverified

cards.name: IVGCloneLink
cards.summary: The link settings of a clone: which master it follows (CloneParent) and which attributes are still linked to it (fill, outline, shape geometry, transform, bitmap colour mask), each a read/write flag; RestoreAllLinks reconnects all of them.
use_for: repeated badges or icons that update when the master changes while one copy keeps its own colour
finding clones in a layout that have drifted from their master before a final revision
re-syncing overridden clones back to the master in one step
avoid: reusable artwork across documents, or many instances with no per-copy overrides: use Symbols instead
shapes that are not clones: Shape.CloneLink has nothing to report
cards.how: Shape.CloneLink on a clone (made with Shape.Clone / CloneAsRange or Edit > Clone). The master is CloneLink.CloneParent; the master lists its clones in Shape.Clones. The *Linked flags are read/write.

key_members.name: CloneParent
key_members.use: the master shape this clone follows

key_members.name: FillLinked
key_members.use: True while the fill follows the master

key_members.name: OutlineLinked
key_members.use: True while the outline follows the master

key_members.name: ShapeLinked
key_members.use: True while the geometry follows the master

key_members.name: TransformLinked
key_members.use: True while size / rotation / skew follow the master

key_members.name: BitmapColorMaskLinked
key_members.use: True while a bitmap colour mask follows the master

key_members.name: RestoreAllLinks
key_members.use: reconnect every attribute to the master

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the clone shape itself

key_members.name: Application
key_members.use: the CorelDRAW application

gotchas: Parent is the clone itself; the master is CloneParent
setting a fill or outline directly on the clone breaks that link (FillLinked / OutlineLinked turn False) (unverified)
setting a *Linked flag back to True should re-take the master's attribute, as RestoreAllLinks does for all (unverified)
Shape.CloneLink on a shape that is not a clone returns Nothing or raises (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim m As Shape, c As Shape
Set m = ActiveShape
Set c = m.Clone(2, 0)
c.Fill.ApplyUniformFill CreateRGBColor(230, 57, 70)
Debug.Print c.CloneLink.FillLinked, c.CloneLink.CloneParent.Name
c.CloneLink.RestoreAllLinks

review.changes: summary no longer states as fact that editing the clone breaks a link (the gotcha keeps that as unverified)

cards.name: IVGColor
cards.summary: A colour value in any CorelDRAW colour model (RGB, CMYK, CMY, HSB, HLS, Lab, YIQ, gray, black-and-white, registration, spot or palette colour, colour style), with its colour context; it is what fills, outlines, fountain-fill nodes, palettes and effects take and return.
use_for: setting brand colours from exact CMYK, RGB or HEX values
assigning Pantone or other spot colours by palette and name for print
converting artwork colours to CMYK for press or to RGB for screen
preflight checks: out of print gamut, spot or not, colour style or not
mixing tints and blends between two colours
avoid: comparing colours with = or Is: use IsSame, or GetColorDistanceFrom for near matches
UserAssign / UserAssignEx in unattended scripts: they open the modal colour dialog and block
cards.how: Created with Application.CreateRGBColor / CreateCMYKColor / CreateColor(colour string) / CreateSpotColorByName and the other Create*Color calls, or read from Fill.UniformColor, Outline.Color, fountain-fill colours, Palette.Color(i) and Document.SampleColorAtPoint. The *Assign methods set model and values, ConvertTo* switch model, and channel properties (RGBRed, CMYKCyan ...) read or set one channel.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: current colour model as cdrColorType

key_members.name: RGBAssign
key_members.use: set RGB values

key_members.name: CMYKAssign
key_members.use: set CMYK values

key_members.name: HexValue
key_members.use: web RGB value as a hex string, read or write

key_members.name: ConvertToCMYK
key_members.use: switch the colour to CMYK

key_members.name: ConvertToRGB
key_members.use: switch the colour to RGB

key_members.name: ConvertTo
key_members.use: switch to any cdrColorType, optionally through source / destination ColorContexts

key_members.name: SpotAssignByName
key_members.use: assign a spot colour by palette identifier and colour name, optional tint

key_members.name: PaletteAssign
key_members.use: assign a colour from a palette by index

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: colour name (optionally with component values)

key_members.name: IsSpot
key_members.use: True for a spot colour

key_members.name: IsSame
key_members.use: same model and same values as another colour

key_members.name: IsInGamut
key_members.use: True when printable on the current printer gamut

key_members.name: GetCopy
key_members.use: independent copy

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: copy model and values from another colour

key_members.name: BlendWith
key_members.use: mix with another colour by a ratio

key_members.name: ToString
key_members.use: encode the colour as a string

key_members.name: StringAssign
key_members.use: decode a colour string made by ToString

key_members.name: Tint
key_members.use: tint of a spot / palette colour

key_members.name: ColorContext
key_members.use: read-only colour context of this colour

gotchas: channel properties only mean something for the current model: RGBRed on a CMYK colour does not convert it; call ConvertToRGB on a GetCopy first

ConvertTo* and *Assign change the colour object in place; on a colour read from Fill.UniformColor or Outline.Color this changes the object's fill or outline (unverified that it always writes through), so read from a GetCopy
valid channel ranges per model are not in the typelib (every channel is a Long); check them against the colour dialog before writing computed values
FixedAssign, ConvertToFixed, PaletteID and PaletteIndex are hidden legacy members; use SpotAssign / SpotAssignByName / PaletteAssign with a palette identifier
Fill.UniformColor and Outline.Color are propput in the typelib: in VBA assign a Color without Set
Tint only applies when IsTintable is True (spot and palette colours)
cards.example:
Dim c As Color, s As Shape
Set c = CreateCMYKColor(0, 85, 70, 0)
For Each s In ActiveSelectionRange
  s.Fill.ApplyUniformFill c
Next s
Debug.Print c.Name(True), c.HexValue, c.IsInGamut

review.changes: removed channel ranges (0-255 / 0-100) that are not in the batch

cards.name: IVGColorContext
cards.summary: A colour context: the set of ICC profiles (RGB, CMYK, grayscale) plus rendering intent and blending colour model that give a document's or a colour's numbers their meaning. Documents carry one, colours report theirs, and conversions can name a source and a destination context.
use_for: setting up a print document for a specific press CMYK profile
converting a whole document to a client's profile set before handoff
converting a single colour between profiles for a spec sheet
checking which profiles a supplied file uses during preflight
avoid: assigning to Document.ColorContext: the property is read-only; build a copy and apply it with Document.AssignColorContext or ConvertToColorContext
application defaults for new documents: use ColorManager.DefaultColorContext
cards.how: Read from Document.ColorContext, Color.ColorContext or Application / ColorManager.DefaultColorContext; create with Application.CreateColorContext(RGBProfile, CMYKProfile, GrayscaleProfile, RenderingIntent, BlendingColorModel), CreateColorContext2(comma-separated profile names) or ColorProfile.CreateColorContext. Apply to a document with Document.AssignColorContext (keeps numbers) or ConvertToColorContext (keeps appearance).

key_members.name: RGBColorProfile
key_members.use: RGB profile of the context

key_members.name: CMYKColorProfile
key_members.use: CMYK profile of the context

key_members.name: GrayscaleColorProfile
key_members.use: grayscale profile of the context

key_members.name: ColorProfile
key_members.use: profile for a given clrColorModel

key_members.name: RenderingIntent
key_members.use: clrRenderingIntent: perceptual, relative, saturation, absolute, automatic

key_members.name: BlendingColorModel
key_members.use: colour model transparencies and blends are computed in

key_members.name: ColorProfileNameList
key_members.use: comma-separated names of all profiles in the context

key_members.name: ColorProfiles
key_members.use: all profiles of the context as a ColorProfiles collection

key_members.name: ReadOnly
key_members.use: True when this context cannot be modified

key_members.name: GetCopy
key_members.use: editable copy

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: copy everything from another context

key_members.name: Merge
key_members.use: take the non-empty profiles of another context

key_members.use: True when two contexts have the same settings

gotchas: Color.ColorContext and Application.DefaultColorContext return read-only contexts (per the typelib); Document.ColorContext probably does too (unverified): check ReadOnly and edit a GetCopy
AssignColorContext keeps colour numbers and changes how they look; ConvertToColorContext keeps the look and rewrites the numbers: the wrong one silently shifts every colour
the profile properties are propput in the typelib: in VBA assign a ColorProfile without Set
BlendingColorModel sets the colour space transparency and blends are flattened in; a mismatch with the output is a likely cause of colour shifts in transparent areas (unverified)
Merge only copies profiles that are non-empty in the source; it never clears one
cards.example:
Dim cc As ColorContext, pressName As String
pressName = "Press CMYK"  ' full Name of an installed CMYK profile
Set cc = ActiveDocument.ColorContext.GetCopy
cc.CMYKColorProfile = Application.ColorManager.ColorProfiles(pressName)
cc.RenderingIntent = clrRenderRelative
ActiveDocument.ConvertToColorContext cc
Debug.Print ActiveDocument.ColorContext.ColorProfileNameList

review.changes: read-only gotcha now matches the typelib (Color / Application contexts are read-only, Document.ColorContext only non-assignable); example uses a placeholder profile name instead of a specific FOGRA39 name that is not in the harvest

cards.name: IVGColorManagementPolicy
cards.summary: One colour-management policy: what CorelDRAW does with RGB, CMYK and grayscale content whose embedded profile differs from the document's (assign or convert, to the document's baseline profile or the embedded one) and whether to warn about mismatched or missing profiles. The application keeps one policy for opening files and one for import / paste.
use_for: making batch open / import jobs convert supplied artwork to the house profiles automatically
turning off mismatch and missing-profile prompts so unattended jobs do not stall
keeping supplied CMYK numbers untouched for print (assign instead of convert)
avoid: setting one document's profiles: use a ColorContext with Document.AssignColorContext / ConvertToColorContext
cards.how: Application.ColorManager.PolicyForOpen and PolicyForImport (application defaults), or StructColorConversionOptions.ColorPolicy for one operation. Each Action* property takes a clrColorPolicyAction: clrAssignBaselineProfile, clrConvertToBaselineProfile, clrConvertToEmbeddedProfile or clrAssignEmbeddedProfile.

key_members.name: ActionForRGB
key_members.use: what to do with RGB content (clrColorPolicyAction)

key_members.name: ActionForCMYK
key_members.use: what to do with CMYK content (clrColorPolicyAction)

key_members.name: ActionForGrayscale
key_members.use: what to do with grayscale content (clrColorPolicyAction)

key_members.name: WarnOnMismatchedProfiles
key_members.use: show a warning when profiles differ

key_members.name: WarnOnMissingProfiles
key_members.use: show a warning when a file has no profile

gotchas: with WarnOnMismatchedProfiles / WarnOnMissingProfiles True, opening or importing can raise a modal dialog that hangs a scripted run; switch them off for batch work and restore them after (unverified that every case prompts)
PolicyForOpen / PolicyForImport are application-wide defaults that persist into later sessions (unverified); save the old values and put them back
'baseline' in the enum names means the document's own colour context profile (unverified)
convert actions rewrite the CMYK numbers of supplied print files; assign actions keep them
cards.example:
Dim p As ColorManagementPolicy, oldWarn As Boolean, oldCMYK As clrColorPolicyAction
Set p = Application.ColorManager.PolicyForImport
oldWarn = p.WarnOnMismatchedProfiles: oldCMYK = p.ActionForCMYK
p.WarnOnMismatchedProfiles = False
p.ActionForCMYK = clrAssignBaselineProfile
' ... import the supplied files ...
p.WarnOnMismatchedProfiles = oldWarn: p.ActionForCMYK = oldCMYK

review.changes: example now saves and restores the application-wide policy, as the card's own gotcha requires

cards.name: IVGColorManager
cards.summary: Application-wide colour management: the installed ICC profile lists, the default colour context for new documents, saved colour-management styles (presets), the colour engine, pure-black and gray-to-K options, spot colour definition and the open / import policies.
use_for: switching CorelDRAW to a saved colour-settings preset before a print batch
finding installed CMYK profiles by colour model or device to build a document colour context
setting PreservePureBlack / MapGrayToCMYKBlack so black text stays 100 K on press
checking which colour engine is active when troubleshooting colour shifts
avoid: one document's profiles: use Document.ColorContext with AssignColorContext / ConvertToColorContext
the hidden legacy members (MonitorCalibration, ShowOutOfGamut, CurrentProfile, InstalledProfiles ...): use the visible members instead
cards.how: Application.ColorManager (one per application). ColorProfiles, GetProfilesByColorModel, GetProfilesForDevice and MonitorColorProfiles return ColorProfiles collections; DefaultColorContext is the context new documents get; LoadStyle / SaveStyle / DeleteStyle manage presets listed by StyleCount and StyleByIndex; PolicyForOpen / PolicyForImport hold the policies.

key_members.name: ColorProfiles
key_members.use: every ICC profile installed on the system

key_members.name: GetProfilesByColorModel
key_members.use: profiles of one clrColorModel (RGB, CMYK, grayscale ...)

key_members.name: GetProfilesForDevice
key_members.use: profiles for a clrDeviceType, optionally one device

key_members.name: MonitorColorProfiles
key_members.use: one profile per installed monitor

key_members.name: DefaultColorContext
key_members.use: context new documents get; editable

key_members.name: StyleCount
key_members.use: number of colour-management styles

key_members.name: StyleByIndex
key_members.use: style name by index

key_members.name: LoadStyle
key_members.use: apply a style by name; returns success

key_members.name: SaveStyle
key_members.use: save current settings as a style

key_members.name: DeleteStyle
key_members.use: delete a style

key_members.name: CanDeleteStyle
key_members.use: False for built-in styles

key_members.name: ColorEngine
key_members.use: colour engine in use (clrColorEngine)

key_members.name: ColorEnginePresent
key_members.use: True when an engine is installed

key_members.name: PreservePureBlack
key_members.use: keep 100 K black as pure black in conversions

key_members.name: MapGrayToCMYKBlack
key_members.use: map grayscale to the CMYK black channel

key_members.name: SpotColorDefinition
key_members.use: which values define spot colours (clrColorModel)

key_members.name: PolicyForOpen
key_members.use: policy applied when opening files

key_members.name: PolicyForImport
key_members.use: policy applied when importing or pasting

gotchas: every setting here is application-wide and outlives the script (unverified that all persist to the next session); record and restore what you change
23 of the 41 members are hidden (calibration, out-of-gamut warning, import / export profiles and colour correction); they may do nothing in version 25 (unverified)
LoadStyle / SaveStyle / DeleteStyle return a Boolean; check it rather than assuming the style exists (unverified whether a bad name raises instead)
the index base of StyleByIndex is not confirmed and style names may be localised; do not hard-code them (unverified)
only set ColorEngine to an engine for which ColorEnginePresent is True
cards.example:
Dim cm As ColorManager, oldBlack As Boolean
Set cm = Application.ColorManager
Debug.Print cm.StyleCount, cm.ColorEngine, cm.GetProfilesByColorModel(clrColorModelCMYK).Count
oldBlack = cm.PreservePureBlack
cm.PreservePureBlack = True
' ... run the print batch ...
cm.PreservePureBlack = oldBlack

review.changes: hidden-member count corrected from "about 25" to 23 of 41; removed "pre-X4" and "2024" (not in the batch); example no longer saves a permanent style and now restores the setting it changes

cards.name: IVGColorProfile
cards.summary: One ICC colour profile as CorelDRAW sees it: full name, file, maker, device model and type, colour model (RGB, CMYK, grayscale, Lab), a unique ID, and whether it is installed on the system or only embedded in a document. All facts are read-only.
use_for: picking the press CMYK profile for a print document's colour context
listing which profiles a supplied file uses during preflight
building a colour context from one profile for a conversion
avoid: changing a profile: everything is read-only, pick a different profile instead
Select / Selected / Generic: hidden legacy device-profile members; set profiles through ColorContext and ColorManager.DefaultColorContext
cards.how: Returned by ColorContext.RGBColorProfile / CMYKColorProfile / GrayscaleColorProfile / ColorProfile(model) and by ColorProfiles.Item(index or full name) from ColorManager.ColorProfiles, GetProfilesByColorModel or GetProfilesForDevice. CreateColorContext(intent) wraps it in a ColorContext.

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: full profile name

key_members.name: FileName
key_members.use: profile file name

key_members.name: ID
key_members.use: unique identifier string

key_members.name: ColorModel
key_members.use: clrColorModel of the profile

key_members.name: DeviceType
key_members.use: clrDeviceType (display, output, input, colour space)

key_members.name: Manufacturer
key_members.use: device maker

key_members.name: DeviceModel
key_members.use: device model

key_members.name: Installed
key_members.use: False when the profile exists only embedded in a document

key_members.name: CreateColorContext
key_members.use: new ColorContext using this profile

key_members.name: IsSame
key_members.use: True when two profiles are the same

gotchas: Installed = False means the profile only lives embedded in a document; it will not be in ColorManager.ColorProfiles
compare profiles with IsSame or ID rather than Name (unverified that names can collide)
ColorProfiles.Item by name needs the full Name exactly as listed
CreateColorContext from one profile fills only that model's slot; Merge it into a full context before converting a document (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim p As ColorProfile
For Each p In Application.ColorManager.GetProfilesByColorModel(clrColorModelCMYK)
  Debug.Print p.Name, p.FileName, p.Installed
Next p

review.changes: none

cards.name: IVGColorProfiles
cards.summary: A collection of ICC colour profiles (all installed ones, those for one device or colour model, the monitors' profiles, or those in a colour context), indexable by position or full profile name, with Install to add a profile file.
use_for: finding a press profile by name to set up a print document
listing available CMYK or RGB profiles in a macro's profile picker
installing a client-supplied ICC profile before converting their job
avoid: SelectByName / GenericProfile: hidden legacy device-profile members; set profiles through ColorContext instead
cards.how: Returned by ColorManager.ColorProfiles, GetProfilesByColorModel(model), GetProfilesForDevice(device), MonitorColorProfiles and ColorContext.ColorProfiles. Item(IndexOrName) is the default member; For Each works via _NewEnum; Install(FileName) adds an .icc / .icm file.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: profile by index or full name (default member)

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of profiles

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets VBA For Each walk the profiles

key_members.name: DeviceType
key_members.use: device type the list was made for

key_members.name: Install
key_members.use: install a profile file; returns success

gotchas: Item by name needs the profile's full Name; a wrong name probably raises rather than returning Nothing (unverified)
Install copies the profile into the Windows colour folder and may need administrator rights (unverified)
a returned collection may be a snapshot: re-read ColorManager.ColorProfiles after Install (unverified)
index base of Item is not confirmed; For Each avoids it (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim cps As ColorProfiles
Set cps = Application.ColorManager.ColorProfiles
Debug.Print cps.Count
If cps.Install("C:\Profiles\ClientPress.icc") Then Debug.Print "installed"

review.changes: none

cards.name: IVGColors
cards.summary: A read-only, 1-based list of Color objects: the colours of one palette (Palette.Colors) or all colour styles of a document (StyleSheet.AllColorStyles).
use_for: exporting a brand palette's colour values to a spec sheet
checking a palette for non-CMYK or out-of-gamut colours before print
looping over a document's colour styles to audit or recolour a layout
avoid: adding or removing colours: the collection has no Add / Remove; use Palette.AddColor / InsertColor
cards.how: Palette.Colors() (from Application.ActivePalette, Application.Palettes or Document.Palette) or Document.StyleSheet.AllColorStyles. Item(Index) is the default member (base 1); For Each works via _NewEnum.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: colour by 1-based index (default member)

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of colours

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets VBA For Each walk the colours

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the Palette, or Nothing for colours not from a palette

key_members.name: Application
key_members.use: the CorelDRAW application

gotchas: Parent is the Palette, or Nothing for colours that are not from a palette (probably the colour-style list, unverified)
Item is 1-based (per the typelib description)
the Color objects may be live references into the palette or colour style: converting them can change the entry; use GetCopy for analysis (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim c As Color
For Each c In Application.ActivePalette.Colors
  If Not c.IsCMYK And Not c.IsSpot Then Debug.Print c.Name, c.Type
Next c

review.changes: marked the colour-style Parent = Nothing inference as unverified

cards.name: IVGComment
cards.summary: One entry in a review comment thread (the Comments docker): its text, author, creation and modification times, GUID and type (cdrCommonComment, cdrResolvedComment or cdrReopenedComment).
use_for: exporting client review comments to a checklist or spreadsheet
finding unanswered feedback before sending a final proof
posting automatic preflight notes as comments on a page
avoid: notes that must print or export with the artwork: comments are review markup; use a text object on a non-printing layer instead (unverified that comments never export)
cards.how: Items of CommentThread.Comments (threads from Page.Markup.Threads); also returned by PageMarkup.CreateHotspot / CreateRectangle / CreateEllipse / CreateArrow / CreateFreehand / CreateHighlight / CreateCollaborativeText, by CommentThread.Reply and by Document.Markup.FindComment(guid). VGCore has no Comment coclass, so declare variables As Object (or IVGComment).

key_members.name: Text
key_members.use: comment text, read / write

key_members.name: Author
key_members.use: CommentAuthor who wrote it

key_members.name: CreationTime
key_members.use: when it was created

key_members.name: ModificationTime
key_members.use: when it was last edited

key_members.name: Guid
key_members.use: unique id, usable with Markup.FindComment and Comments.Item

key_members.name: Thread
key_members.use: the CommentThread it belongs to

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrCommentType: cdrCommonComment, cdrResolvedComment, cdrReopenedComment

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: delete it (the whole thread if it is the first comment)

gotchas: Delete on the first comment of a thread deletes the whole thread
Author is putref in the typelib: in VBA write Set c.Author = ... with an object from Application.CreateMarkupAuthor
resolve / reopen events appear to be stored as comments of Type cdrResolvedComment / cdrReopenedComment (unverified); filter on cdrCommonComment when exporting feedback text
ReadBy, ReadByCount, UserAssigned, UserAssignedCount, AddReadBy, AddUserAssigned and OnlineID are hidden cloud-collaboration members (unverified in local files)
cards.example:
Dim t As Object, c As Object
For Each t In ActivePage.Markup.Threads
  For Each c In t.Comments
    If c.Type = cdrCommonComment Then Debug.Print c.Author.Name, c.CreationTime, c.Text
  Next c
Next t

review.changes: summary no longer asserts that resolved / reopened types are status entries (gotcha marked unverified); hidden-member list completed (ReadByCount, UserAssignedCount); added PageMarkup.CreateCollaborativeText to the access paths

cards.name: IVGCommentAnnotation
cards.summary: The on-canvas mark of a comment thread: a hotspot pin, rectangle, ellipse, arrow, freehand line, highlight or co-editing mark, with its outline width and colours, arrowhead visibility, path, and position / size on the page.
use_for: drawing review marks (circle, arrow, highlight) on a proof from a script
moving review pins after the artwork was laid out again
listing where on the page each piece of feedback points
avoid: callouts that must print: annotations are review markup; draw ordinary shapes for printed callouts (unverified that they never print)
cards.how: CommentThread.Annotation. Its kind is fixed by the PageMarkup.Create* call that made the thread (Type returns a cdrCommentAnnotationType). Position and size members mirror Shape's (LeftX ... CenterY, SetPosition, SetSize, Move, GetBoundingBox / SetBoundingBox).

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrCommentAnnotationType: freehand, hotspot, arrow, highlight, rectangle, ellipse, co-editing

key_members.name: Curve
key_members.use: the mark's path, when it has one

key_members.name: OutlineWidth
key_members.use: stroke width (Long)

key_members.name: OutlineColor
key_members.use: stroke colour

key_members.name: FillColor
key_members.use: fill colour

key_members.name: StartArrowVisible
key_members.use: arrowhead at the start of an arrow mark

key_members.name: EndArrowVisible
key_members.use: arrowhead at the end of an arrow mark

key_members.name: Move
key_members.use: shift by DeltaX / DeltaY

key_members.name: SetPosition
key_members.use: move a reference point to x, y

key_members.name: GetPosition
key_members.use: read a reference point's x, y (ByRef)

key_members.name: SetSize
key_members.use: stretch to a width and height from a reference point

key_members.name: GetBoundingBox
key_members.use: read x, y, width, height (ByRef)

key_members.name: SetBoundingBox
key_members.use: move and resize into a box

key_members.name: LeftX
key_members.use: left edge

key_members.name: TopY
key_members.use: top edge

key_members.name: CenterX
key_members.use: horizontal centre

key_members.name: CenterY
key_members.use: vertical centre

key_members.name: SizeWidth
key_members.use: width

key_members.name: SizeHeight
key_members.use: height

gotchas: OutlineWidth is a Long (whole numbers) unlike a shape's Outline.Width; its unit is not documented (unverified)
Type is read-only: to turn a rectangle mark into an arrow, delete the thread and create a new one with PageMarkup.CreateArrow

GetPosition / GetSize / GetBoundingBox return values through out (ByRef) parameters per the typelib (GetPosition's ReferencePoint is an input); in Python win32com they should come back as a tuple (unverified)
FillColor / OutlineColor / Curve are propput in the typelib: in VBA assign without Set
size members probably mean nothing for a hotspot pin (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim t As Object
For Each t In ActivePage.Markup.Threads
  With t.Annotation
    Debug.Print .Type, .CenterX, .CenterY
    If .Type = cdrCommentAnnotationArrow Then .EndArrowVisible = True
  End With
Next t

review.changes: ByRef gotcha now states the typelib out-parameter flags, including that GetPosition's ReferencePoint is an input

cards.name: IVGCommentAuthor
cards.summary: The identity attached to review comments: display name, email, avatar and how the author signed in (unauthenticated guest, Google, Microsoft or CDA, per cdrAuthorAuthentication). All fields are read-only.
use_for: stamping script-generated review comments with a bot or reviewer name
grouping exported feedback by reviewer
setting the identity used for new comments with Application.MarkupLogin
avoid: renaming an existing author: the fields are read-only; create a new identity with Application.CreateMarkupAuthor
cards.how: Comment.Author on existing comments; new identities come from Application.CreateMarkupAuthor(Name, Avatar, Email, Authentication). Passed as the optional Author argument of PageMarkup.Create*, CommentThread.Reply / Resolve / Reopen, or made the current user with Application.MarkupLogin. No coclass: declare As Object.

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: display name

key_members.name: Email
key_members.use: email address

key_members.name: Avatar
key_members.use: avatar string (image reference)

key_members.name: Authentication
key_members.use: cdrAuthorAuthentication: guest, GSuite, O365, CDA or undefined

gotchas: Name, Email, Avatar and Authentication are read-only
use cdrAuthorAuthenticationGuest for local scripts; the GSuite / O365 / CDA values describe signed-in cloud identities and are not checked by CreateMarkupAuthor (unverified)
what Avatar accepts (file path or URL) is not documented (unverified)
Comment.Author is putref in the typelib: use Set in VBA
cards.example:
Dim a As Object
Set a = Application.CreateMarkupAuthor("Preflight Bot", "", "preflight@example.com", cdrAuthorAuthenticationGuest)
ActivePage.Markup.CreateHotspot "Image below 300 dpi", 2, 8, a

review.changes: summary no longer expands CDA to "Corel account" (the harvest only says "Authenticated via CDA")

cards.name: IVGComments
cards.summary: The comments inside one review thread, in order: the opening comment, its replies, and resolve / reopen entries. Look one up by index or by its GUID; First and Last give the opening comment and the latest entry.
use_for: reading the full discussion on one piece of feedback
getting the latest reply of each thread for a status report
jumping to a comment by GUID from an exported review list
avoid: adding a reply: there is no Add, use CommentThread.Reply
listing all threads on a page: that is PageMarkup.Threads
cards.how: CommentThread.Comments (thread from Page.Markup.Threads or Document.Markup.FindThread). Item(IndexOrGuid) is the default member; For Each works via _NewEnum.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: comment by index or Guid string (default member)

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of comments in the thread

key_members.name: First
key_members.use: the comment that opened the thread

key_members.name: Last
key_members.use: the newest entry

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets VBA For Each walk the comments

gotchas: Item accepts either an index or the comment's Guid string
First is the comment that opened the thread; deleting it deletes the whole thread
resolve / reopen events are comments too and count in Count, so Last may be a status entry, not a reply (unverified)

the typelib describes IVGComments as "a set of comments associated with a document", but the only member that returns it is CommentThread.Comments; for a document-wide lookup by GUID use Document.Markup.FindComment
cards.example:
Dim t As Object
For Each t In ActivePage.Markup.Threads
  Debug.Print t.Comments.Count, t.Comments.First.Text, t.Comments.Last.Author.Name
Next t

review.changes: added a gotcha reconciling the typelib description ("associated with a document") with the only access path, CommentThread.Comments

cards.name: IVGCommentTarget
cards.summary: What a review comment thread is attached to: the shape the thread points at, and that shape's GUID.
use_for: selecting the objects reviewers commented on so a script or designer can fix them
listing which objects in a layout carry feedback
re-pointing a thread to a replacement object after artwork is swapped
avoid: the on-canvas pin or mark position: that is CommentThread.Annotation
cards.how: CommentThread.Target. Shape is the attached Shape; Guid is that shape's GUID string. Both are writable.

key_members.name: Shape
key_members.use: the shape the thread is attached to (putref)

key_members.name: Guid
key_members.use: GUID of that shape

gotchas: Shape is putref in the typelib: in VBA re-target with Set t.Target.Shape = s
Shape is probably Nothing when the comment was placed on empty canvas; test before use (unverified)
Guid and Shape are both writable; set Shape and let Guid follow rather than writing Guid by hand (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim t As Object
For Each t In ActivePage.Markup.Threads
  If Not t.Target.Shape Is Nothing Then t.Target.Shape.AddToSelection
Next t

review.changes: none
